liquidity_funding.text: The group repaid its interest-bearing financial liabilities in full, which the report says greatly reduces the sensitivity of the company to changes in interest rates.
A financing commitment was given to the City Air Terminal joint venture for new train sets, part of which was drawn as a loan in the year.
Total debt was stable at {{total_debt@FY2024}}, so the funding base rests on internally generated cash rather than on drawn borrowings.
Undrawn committed facilities are not disclosed for the year, so the liquidity buffer rests on cash generated and on the absence of interest-bearing financial liabilities.

watch_items.text: Cash generation: free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}} as capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2024}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2024}}, in line with the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@FY2024}}.
Traffic: traffic growth of {{traffic_growth@FY2024}} is below the peer median of {{traffic_growth.peer_median@FY2024}} and the weakest of the group ({{traffic_growth.peer_rank@FY2024}}).
Regulation: airport charges are temporarily adjusted by average inflation, a rule that ends at the end of 2026, so revenue per passenger depends on the tariff application that follows.
Litigation: disputes with the Maltese government and employee claims concerning Malta International Airport were outstanding at the balance sheet date, which the group considers unfounded.
